content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"All three blind responses identify the Holy Spirit (indwelling, anointing, sustaining presence) as the dominant Christian meaning of lamp oil, grounded chiefly in Zechariah 4, the tabernacle lamp texts, anointing narratives, and Matthew 25. Alternatives acknowledged include preparedness/watchfulness, good works or charity, grace, genuine faith, and—only as a minority/rare view—the Word of God or divine instruction. Two responses say there is no fully settled consensus; one says the Spirit reading is settled.","book_summary":"The book defines lamp oil as the commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until it governs the life—the pressed, tested fruit stored as proven obedience—with light being that obedience made visible to others as an example. It explicitly flags the common teaching (Holy Spirit/anointing) as the view it departs from.","rationale":"The book's central claim displaces the dominant Holy Spirit reading with a Word/commandment-internalized-as-obedience referent. This aligns loosely with the consensus responses' minority/rare 'Word of God or spiritual illumination' alternative and partially with the 'good works' alternative (via Matt 5:16), but it is not the leading interpretation in any blind response, and the book itself frames the Spirit reading as the 'commonly taught' view it corrects. Because it contradicts and replaces the recognizable common interpretation rather than sharpening it, DIVERGENT fits better than REFINED or NOVEL (a related minority reading is recognizable, so it is not wholly novel).","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"Zechariah 4:6 ('not by might... but by my spirit') and Ezekiel 36:27 ('I will put my spirit within you'), both printed with the entry, most naturally identify the oil's supply with the Spirit rather than with internalized commandments, and Matthew 25 nowhere equates the oil with laid-up truth; the chain from Ps 141:5 (reproof as oil), Prov 21:20 (oil in the dwelling of the wise), and Prov 23:23 ('buy the truth') is suggestive but associative, requiring the reader to accept lexical linkage across genres as establishing a symbolic definition.","confidence":"high"}
